sentences.text: The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — includes a subadult skeleton with parts of the skull, vertebrae, limb bones, sternal plates, and pelvic elements.
Research indicates that Losillasaurus possessed heart-shaped teeth and exhibited heterodonty, a variation in tooth types within the skull.
The genus is characterized by the dimensions and shape of the neural spines on the proximal caudal vertebrae.
The largest estimated Losillasaurus would have measured 25 meters in length and weighed approximately 47 tonnes.
The humerus of the type specimen measures 143 cm, which is within 20% of the size of Paralititan despite coming from a subadult.

The type species Losillasaurus giganteus was discovered in the Los Serranos comarca in Valencia, Spain, within the Collado Sandstone and Clay Formation and formally described by Casanovas, Santafé, and Sanz in 2001.

Fossils of Losillasaurus have also been found in the Lourinhã Formation of Portugal, and additional specimens were described in 2019 and 2020, including a single anterior caudal vertebra and a partial skull with teeth.
Losillasaurus is classified within the unranked family Turiasauria, and the parent group of Losillasaurus is Turiasauria.

Losillasaurus lived during the Late Jurassic, approximately 154 to 145 million years ago, in what is now Europe, specifically during the Kimmeridgian to Tithonian stages, from 154.8 to 143.1 million years ago.
